description.text: In the Old Forest, the hobbits meet Tom Bombadil—a mysterious and ancient being, seemingly as old as the woods themselves. At the Council of Elrond, the idea of giving the Ring to Tom is discussed, since he is immune to its corruption. Yet he is also immune to its burden and responsibility. Tom cannot be entrusted with the Ring: he would not understand its importance, might forget it entirely, and would never think to guard it.
Amon Sûl, the ancient watchtower where Frodo was wounded by the Morgul blade. The ruins stand lonely on the hilltop, haunted by memories of the Nazgûl's attack.
The Doors of Durin, hidden entrance to the Mines of Moria. 'Speak friend and enter' - a riddle that nearly cost the Fellowship their passage.
The narrow stone arch where Gandalf faced the Balrog. 'You shall not pass!' echoed through the ancient halls as the wizard fell into shadow.
The Pillars of Kings, massive statues of Isildur and Anárion carved from living rock. They guard the northern approach to Gondor, silent witnesses to the passage of time.
A maze of barren hills and twisted ravines where Frodo and Sam became hopelessly lost. Here they first captured Gollum, who would become both guide and nemesis.
An accursed wasteland where the dead of ancient battles lie preserved beneath the water. Pale faces and ghostly lights lure travelers to their doom.
The tunnel of Cirith Ungol, home to Shelob the Great Spider. Ancient and evil, she has dwelt in darkness for ages, feeding on all who dare pass through her domain.
The desolate plain of Mordor, scorched by volcanic heat and poisoned by evil. Across this wasteland, Frodo and Sam made their final desperate march.
